title: Application of existing standards and planning discipline
summary: Make existing instructions actionable and reviewable before and after implementation.
description:
Make existing instructions actionable and reviewable before and after implementation.

Current state: extend existing Agent Plan functionality; see each task for the verified starting point. This phase follows C and owns only the outcomes below.

Outcomes:
- Require relevant source analysis and conformity evidence without duplicating existing guidelines.
- Distribute a consistent protocol across supported agents and limit unnecessary task creation.

Tasks and boundaries:
- D1: Add evidence-backed source analysis and conformity review to existing workflow. An auditable pre-implementation analysis and post-implementation conformity report on the existing task, usable without semantic providers.
- D2: Synchronize the operating protocol across harnesses and context-loss events. One portable operational protocol with explicit adapter capabilities, renewed context and consistent instruction delivery.
- D3: Prevent duplicate capability ownership and unnecessary task creation. A creation workflow that surfaces existing open/completed ownership and keeps implementation steps within the current task.

Preserve canonical planner identity, phase-scoped handoffs, derived status and session ownership. Read existing code precedents before implementation; use the current task checklist for steps. Source locations are navigation evidence at c4d0c459f74f5365c9ab8a9fe53ad6d7907a8231, not permanent anchors.

Acceptance: A new agent produces a component consistent with the correct architectural precedents. Legacy conflicts and greenfield projects are explicit; no fabricated standards or false proof of understanding. No extra permission prompt is introduced for already authorized routine work. Generated skill copies and tool descriptions express one consistent workflow. Every supported harness has a documented tested coverage level and explicit fallback. Loss of model context leads to restoration rather than reuse of a historical timestamp alone. Already owned work reuses its owner; an implementation detail becomes a checklist item. Independent outcomes can still create justified tasks. No arbitrary task-count cap, automatic merges/deletions or one-task-per-stale-link behavior.

Every create/update/move or relationship change checks affected task/phase/feature/project scope and dependency readiness through P128(F025)/T496. Return indexed affected deltas rather than full ancestor/plan/graph reloads; measure per-flow context/payload/tool budgets without dropping mandatory rules or inventing context retention. BR28 and BR29 apply to this phase. Full contract: .planner/docs/agent-brain-impact-reconciliation-and-token-budgets.md.

tasks.title: Prevent duplicate capability ownership and unnecessary task creation
tasks.description:
Outcome: A creation workflow that surfaces existing open/completed ownership and keeps implementation steps within the current task.

Existing state: The skill and phase work map already advise checklist reuse and sibling review; new tasks can still be created without an evidence-backed comparison.

Implementation responsibility:
- Compare requested outcome against relevant canonical tasks, including completed capabilities and cross-phase candidates.
- Use similarity as a discovery hint, never an automatic proof or destructive deduplication.
- Require a distinct outcome and rationale for a new task; otherwise update current checklist/description or capture an out-of-scope idea.
- Keep initialization and legitimate large-feature planning possible; show useful ownership information in current UI.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Already owned work reuses its owner; an implementation detail becomes a checklist item.
- Independent outcomes can still create justified tasks.
- No arbitrary task-count cap, automatic merges/deletions or one-task-per-stale-link behavior.
